judge_assessment.explanation: Both judge observations are accurate. The worksheet PDF carries exactly 10 problems, and I recomputed every one: 3<7, 9>4, 6=6, greater-first 8,5, smaller-first 2,7, 10>8, ascending 4,6,9, Mia 2+3=5 then 5<9, descending 10,7,3, and Sam 6+1=7 versus Ana 9-1=8 giving '<'. All thirteen verify.json checks match the key's boxed values. The 'text-dense for the youngest readers' note is fair. The claim I have to qualify is 'All three artifacts are complete and readable': the answer key's Quick Answers bank reads '1. -  2. -  3. -  4. 8, 5  5. 2, 7  6. -  7. 4, 6, 9  8. 5, -  9. 10, 7, 3  10. 7, 8, -'. Six of the ten entries are bare em-dashes and two more are partial, on a worksheet whose declared subject IS writing <, > and =. The bank exists so a grader can scan the answers, and for the majority of this sheet it carries nothing. Same root cause as curr-001, but the impact here is severe enough that I would not have scored answer_key_quality a full 4.

strengths_to_preserve: verify.json binds every printed response slot on the two multi-part items, which is exactly the pattern the shard-wide verify-every-printed-answer-slot finding asks for and which most sibling cases miss: id 8 carries an eval (n+3 at n=2 -> 5) for the 'Mia's numeral is ___' blank AND a compare (2+3 vs 9) for the box, and id 10 carries three entries (6+1 -> 7, 9-1 -> 8, and the relation) for its three blanks.

The ramp genuinely avoids a repeated skeleton across 10 items: symbol between two numerals (1-3), circle-then-rewrite-in-order (4-5), the two-digit trap 10 vs 8 (6), three-numeral ordering in both directions (7, 9), and count-on-then-compare (8, 10).

Problem 3 puts 6 = 6 into the set. Equality is the case children skip when they learn '<' and '>' as a pair, and the key answers it on its own terms ('neither is said later when counting') rather than by arithmetic.
The shared number line is drawn with no problem values on it and says so in its caption, so no problem can leak a neighbour's answer through the figure.

root_causes.description: scripts/render_quick_answers.py resolves a string 'expected' by sympify+latex and falls back to a TeX em-dash when sympify raises. A bare relation symbol is not a sympifiable expression, so every compare problem whose order is 'relation' is silently banked as '---' — the marker the module documents as 'manual-only / see solution'. The verified answer exists and is correct; the grader's quick-reference column simply refuses to print it.
evidence: answer_key.pdf page 1 Quick Answers: ids 1, 2, 3 and 6 are '-' outright; id 8 is '5, -' and id 10 is '7, 8, -'. Only ids 4, 5, 7 and 9 (the asc/desc orderings, whose expected values are integer lists) render.

verify.json: ids 1, 2, 3, 6 and the trailing entries of ids 8 and 10 all carry "order": "relation" with expected "<", ">" or "="; gate_log.txt step 5 shows all 13 checks PASS, so the values are present and verified.
scripts/render_quick_answers.py _fmt(): sympify('<') and sympify('=') both raise SympifyError and the str branch returns '---'.

root_causes.description: Study-guide skill headings are written by hand and the internal machine skill/facet slug leaks into some of them but not others, so a K-1 student document prints an identifier that means nothing to its reader. SKILL.md requires each study-guide entry to be tagged with the 'skill' it demonstrates but never says the slug must stay out of the printed heading.
evidence: study_guide.tex: '\skillheading{Skill 1 --- Compare with a symbol (compare-with-symbols)}' while Skills 2, 3 and 4 carry no slug — the same document is inconsistent with itself.
verify_study_guide.json tags the same entry "skill": "compare-with-symbols", so the slug in the heading is a duplicate of machine metadata that the coverage gate already reads from the JSON.
The same leak appears in sibling cases: curr-051 tags all four headings ('1. Reading a model (read-base-ten-model)'), curr-045 tags two of three, curr-023 tags two of three.

improvements.title: Quick Answers bank prints an em-dash instead of the verified relation symbol
improvements.proposed_change: In scripts/render_quick_answers.py, handle relation strings in _fmt() BEFORE the sympify attempt: map '<', '>', '=', '<=', '>=', '!=' (and the unicode forms) to '$<$', '$>$', '$=$', '$\le$', '$\ge$', '$\ne$'. sympy.sympify('<') raises SympifyError, so today every compare entry with "order": "relation" drops into the '---' fallback that exists for genuinely unrenderable values. Keep '---' for manual-only ids and for real sympify failures, so the fallback still means 'see the worked solution'.
improvements.regression_test: Add a case to tests/test_render_quick_answers.py that renders a verify JSON of [{'id':1,'type':'compare','values':['3','7'],'order':'relation','expected':'<'}, {'id':2,'type':'compare','values':['9','4'],'order':'relation','expected':'>'}, {'id':3,'type':'manual','desc':'open'}] and asserts the bank lines are '$<$', '$>$' and '---' respectively. Today entries 1 and 2 both render '---', so the assertion fails; after the relation mapping it passes, and the manual id still prints '---'.
improvements.expected_impact: Restores 6 fully missing and 2 partial entries out of 10 on this sheet, turning an unusable grading column into a usable one. Across the shard the same one-line fix repairs every compare-heavy answer key (curr-001, curr-034, curr-045 and curr-051 all ship em-dashes for their relation items).
improvements.risk: Low. Bank entries stay plain text (no \ans/\boxed), so check_answer_key.py's strict per-problem boxed-answer binding is untouched, and column_count() only sees a 3-char string. The only judgement call is math-mode wrapping of '='; both '=' and '$=$' set correctly inside the multicols block.

improvements.title: Internal skill/facet slugs are printed in student-facing study-guide headings
improvements.proposed_change: State in SKILL.md's study-guide section that \skillheading text is student prose and must not contain the machine 'skill'/'facet' slug — the slug lives in verify_ss_*.json, which is where the coverage gate reads it from. Then add the check to tests/check_study_guide.py: for each \skillheading, exit 2 if the heading text contains a lowercase-hyphenated token equal to any 'skill' or 'facet' value in the paired verify JSON.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture study guide whose first heading is '\skillheading{Skill 1 --- Compare with a symbol (compare-with-symbols)}' paired with a verify JSON tagging that entry "skill": "compare-with-symbols": the checker must exit non-zero and name heading 1. A second fixture with the heading '\skillheading{Skill 1 --- Compare with a symbol}' and the same JSON must exit 0. Today both fixtures pass, so the first assertion fails before the fix.
improvements.expected_impact: Student-facing documents stop printing internal identifiers, and the inconsistency inside a single guide (Skill 1 tagged, Skills 2-4 not) disappears. Cosmetic only — no answer or verification changes.
improvements.risk: Low, but the matcher must be anchored to the paired JSON's own slug values rather than to any hyphenated word, or a legitimate heading such as 'Count-on to add' would false-fail.

case_summary: Ten mathematically correct, well-ramped numeral-comparison problems with the best verification coverage in my batch: the two multi-blank items carry one verify entry per printed slot (id 8 twice, id 10 three times), so nothing a student writes goes unchecked. The failure is downstream of that good work. Because the Quick Answers renderer cannot sympify a relation symbol, the answer key's grading column prints an em-dash for six of ten problems on a sheet about writing <, > and =. A minor second issue: Skill 1's study-guide heading leaks the internal slug '(compare-with-symbols)' while the other three headings do not.
